findings.claim: The user_location cleanup only deletes rows for the location passed to deleteLocation, but Location.childLocations is mapped cascade=ALL/orphanRemoval=true (Location.java:140), so descendants that Hibernate deletes by cascade keep their user_location rows and the purge fails on the FK.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, purging a parent location (e.g. a department) whose child is assigned to a user throws ConstraintViolationException on the user_location_to_location FK, because Hibernate cascades the child delete without passing through deleteLocation. The ticket says user_location stores resolved leaf locations under departments, so this is exactly the hierarchy deployments will have. The same applies when a child is removed via orphanRemoval.
findings.evidence: Temporary probe in LocationServiceTest (reverted): create parent+child via parent.addChildLocation, saveLocation, flush; assign child to user 1, saveUser, flush+clear; purgeLocation(parent); flushSession -> ConstraintViolationException 'Referential integrity constraint violation: FKC0WEUGWTYIDBYTMDYE09CP0GL: PUBLIC.USER_LOCATION FOREIGN KEY(LOCATION_ID) REFERENCES PUBLIC.LOCATION(LOCATION_ID) (11)'. Control (same setup without the assignment) passes. Run: mvn -o -B -pl api -am test -Dtest='LocationServiceTest#probe*+purgeLocation*'. Fix options: delete user_location rows for the location and its descendants (the DAO already has a recursive CTE in getDescendantIds), or put ON DELETE CASCADE on the location_id FK in the changeset (note the unit-test H2 schema comes from hbm2ddl, FK name is Hibernate-generated, so a Liquibase-only cascade would not be exercised by unit tests).

findings.claim: The native delete declares no synchronized query space, so Hibernate invalidates every second-level cache region (users, concepts, ...) on each purgeLocation; adding .addSynchronizedQuerySpace("user_location") scopes it.
findings.evidence: Probe: load User 1 and Concept 3 into L2, clear session, purgeLocation(location 6), check sessionFactory.getCache().containsEntity: PR head prints 'user true->false concept true->false'; with the native delete removed prints 'true->true' (calibration); with .addSynchronizedQuerySpace("user_location") added prints 'true->true' and all purgeLocation* tests still pass (Hibernate 7.4.7, hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache=true in hibernate.default.properties:33). User.locations has no @Cache, so no collection region needs evicting.

findings.claim: purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser never flushes, so it passes with the user_location fix removed and does not guard the regression it was added for.
findings.evidence: Mutation run: removed the native delete in HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation; purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser still passed, while a variant that does flushSession()+clearSession() after saveUser and flushSession() after purgeLocation failed with the user_location FK violation (and passes with the fix in place). Adding only a flush to the test as written (user still loaded in session) fails at flush with TransientPropertyValueException 'Persistent instance of org.openmrs.User references an unsaved transient instance of org.openmrs.Location [User.locations]' even with the fix, i.e. the test itself holds a loaded User across the purge, the exact situation the new comment at HibernateLocationDAO.java:129-132 says no caller does.

findings.claim: User.locations is LAZY and is not hydrated where roles/userProperties/privileges are (HibernateContextDAO.authenticate ~L166-168, UserContext.becomeUser ~L184-195), so getLocations() on Context.getAuthenticatedUser() throws LazyInitializationException in any later session; is that intended given the companion REST PR exposes locations on the user resource?
findings.evidence: Probe: flushSession+clearSession, then Context.getAuthenticatedUser(): getAllRoles().size() returns 1 (control), getLocations().size() throws org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException. Core itself does not call getLocations on the authenticated user (getAllowedLocations re-reads via dao.getUser), so no in-repo breakage; whether the REST companion (#762) serializes it could not be checked here.

findings.claim: getAllowedLocations takes an arbitrary User and requires only GET_LOCATIONS, and loads it via dao.getUser, so a caller without GET_USERS can learn any user's location assignments; should it require GET_USERS for another user, or be scoped to the authenticated user?
findings.evidence: Read UserService.java:668-669 (@Authorized(GET_LOCATIONS)) vs UserService.getUser @Authorized(GET_USERS) at UserService.java:86-87; UserServiceImpl.java:860 calls dao.getUser directly. Not run: whether the REST layer adds its own check is in the companion PR.

verdict: Not ready: the user_location FK cleanup misses locations deleted by Hibernate's child-location cascade, so purging a parent location with an assigned descendant fails, and the added regression test cannot catch either this or the original bug because it never flushes.
